STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple on a white square plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is square with rounded corners, about 24 cm across (roughly a dinner/salad plate). Its area is about 24 x 24 = 576 cm², minus the corners, so ~540 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One whole red-orange apple (Pink Lady or Gala type). There is no other food.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple is about 128 px wide against a plate width of about 345 px, which gives 128/345 x 24 ≈ 8.9 cm. Its footprint is π x 4.45² ≈ 62 cm², or about 11% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere of diameter ~8.5 cm has volume 4/3 x π x 4.25³ ≈ 320 ml. The apple is slightly flattened, so I use ~290 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole apple has a density of about 0.8 g/ml, because of its air pockets. 290 x 0.8 ≈ 230 g. An apple 8.5 cm across typically weighs 200–230 g, so I take ~215 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 215 g gives ≈ 112 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium-large apple at ~215 g and ~110 kcal is plausible.
